findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on I/O result panics on missing/unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or absent file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed domain error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and propagate io::Error via ? or explicit map_err

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string) is embedded directly in the same function as parsing and domain construction — no separation of imperative shell from pure core
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test parsing logic without involving the filesystem; side effects are hidden inside what looks like a data-processing function
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell fn load_samples(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> that does I/O, and (2) pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseErr> that processes lines

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O side effect (logging) inside a mapping function that should be pure data transformation
findings.failure_mode: pure core code emits side effects, making behavior non-deterministic and non-testable; output order depends on iteration order and may interleave in parallel contexts
findings.fix: remove println! from the core pipeline; move all logging to the imperative shell boundary

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on numeric parse panics on non-numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (e.g., "abc" in value field) crashes the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result and use map_err to convert ParseIntError into a domain error type

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into parts Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics with IndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.fix: use get(1).ok_or(ParseErr::MissingField) or split_once(',') and handle the None case

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into parts Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: an empty line or line with no comma panics with IndexOutOfBoundsException

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() — uses split + collect + indexing when split_once suffices for the two-field CSV grammar
findings.failure_mode: allocates a full Vec of all fields unnecessarily; also masks the two-field constraint because any split count silently proceeds until unchecked index access
findings.fix: use split_once(',') for first-delimiter extraction, trim each half, and handle the None case

findings.problem: (u32) as u16 — lossy cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values outside 0..=65535
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 silently wraps to 4464, producing incorrect data with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(u32_val) and return a domain error on overflow; or parse directly as u16: parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: load_samples performs I/O, parsing, validation, logging, and domain construction in a single function — no functional core / imperative shell separation
findings.failure_mode: every caller must handle IO errors; pure logic cannot be tested in isolation; hidden side effects make the function non-deterministic
findings.fix: extract: shell fn load_samples(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>; pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>; move println! to shell

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocated for every line with no try_reserve or capacity planning — each line allocates a new Vec plus multiple String allocations
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations on every line; in high-throughput or memory-constrained contexts this causes allocation pressure and potential OOM
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to avoid Vec allocation; use &str references with trim; only allocate Strings for the final Record fields

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for any performance claims or allocation behavior of load_samples
findings.failure_mode: undetermined whether this function meets throughput, latency, or memory-budget requirements; cargo-cult patterns may be hiding inefficiencies
findings.fix: add a Criterion benchmark measuring allocations, throughput, and latency for typical and adversarial CSV inputs

findings.problem: No domain error type defined — raw io::Error, ParseIntError, and IndexError propagate through unwrap() with no typed error taxonomy
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot pattern-match on specific failure modes; no railway-oriented error handling; all errors are opaque panics
findings.fix: define a domain Error enum (e.g., LoadError { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), MissingField { line: usize } }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>
